accepted.reviewerNote: Drops 'fermentation' branch and 'stringy'; use 'a stringy mix of yeast and bacteria that forms during fermentation and turns cider or wine into vinegar.'

accepted.definition: a woman who has given birth to a child (also used as a term of address to your mother)
accepted.simpleMeaning: a woman who has a child of her own, also used when you speak to her.
accepted.scope: This is not the slimy substance used in vinegar-making, nor the act of caring for someone; it is a woman with a child.
examples: My mother taught me how to cook.
She became a mother at the age of thirty.
branchCoverage: a woman who has given birth to a child (also used as a term of address to your mother) -> a woman who has a child of her own, also used when you speak to her
accepted.lemmaPartition: mother (noun, vinegar) = a slimy mix of yeast and bacteria used to make vinegar; mother (noun, parent) = a woman who has a child; mother (verb) = to care for someone in a kind, protective way.

accepted.definition: care for like a mother
accepted.simpleMeaning: to care for someone in a kind, protective way.
accepted.scope: This is not being a female parent; it means looking after someone with special care.
examples: She mothered the new students until they felt at home.
He mothered his younger brother through the illness.
branchCoverage: care for like a mother -> to care for someone in a kind, protective way
accepted.lemmaPartition: mother (noun, vinegar) = a slimy mix of yeast and bacteria used to make vinegar; mother (noun, parent) = a woman who has a child; mother (verb) = to care for someone in a kind, protective way.

accepted.definition: the territorial and administrative division of some countries (such as France)
accepted.simpleMeaning: a large area of a country that has its own local government.
accepted.scope: This is not a group of workers in a company or a part of a shop; it is a large area of a country with its own local government.
examples: The country is divided into departments, each with its own council.
They travelled through several departments on their way south.
branchCoverage: the territorial and administrative division of some countries (such as France) -> a large area of a country that has its own local government

accepted.definition: an aggressive willingness to compete
accepted.simpleMeaning: a strong wish to compete and win.
accepted.scope: This is not a physical battle or an argument; it is the strong wish to compete and win.
examples: There was real fight in the team during the second half.
She showed great fight and refused to give up the match.
branchCoverage: an aggressive willingness to compete -> a strong wish to compete and win
accepted.lemmaPartition: fight (noun, spirit) = a strong wish to compete and win; fight (noun, act) = an act of using force or a hard struggle; fight (verb) = to struggle hard against someone or something.

accepted.definition: the act of fighting; any contest or struggle
accepted.simpleMeaning: an act of using force against someone, or a hard struggle.
accepted.scope: This is not the strong wish to compete; it is the act itself, or a hard struggle.
examples: A fight broke out outside the pub.
The fight against poverty will take many years.
branchCoverage: the act of fighting -> an act of using force against someone
any contest or struggle -> a hard struggle
accepted.lemmaPartition: fight (noun, spirit) = a strong wish to compete and win; fight (noun, act) = an act of using force or a hard struggle; fight (verb) = to struggle hard against someone or something.

accepted.definition: fight against or resist strongly
accepted.simpleMeaning: to struggle hard against someone or something.
accepted.scope: This is not taking part in a physical battle; it means resisting or opposing something with all your strength.
examples: The villagers fought against the new road for years.
She fought hard to keep her business open.
branchCoverage: fight against or resist strongly -> to struggle hard against someone or something
accepted.lemmaPartition: fight (noun, spirit) = a strong wish to compete and win; fight (noun, act) = an act of using force or a hard struggle; fight (verb) = to struggle hard against someone or something.
